songInfo.title: When I Come Around
songInfo.tuning: Half-Step Down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

scalesUsed.notes: G - A - B - C - D - E - F#
scalesUsed.application: Drives the iconic four-chord progression and Billie Joe Armstrong's melodic guitar solo
Forms the clean, singable core of the lead fills and vocal harmonies
Provides bluesy inflections and gritty micro-bends during the solo turnaround

keyAndScale.keySignature: One sharp (F#) (concert F# major due to half-step down tuning)

mainProgression.description: One of the most celebrated four-chord progressions in modern rock history. Billie Joe Armstrong voices the chords as punchy power chords while allowing the open high strings to ring intermittently, creating a chiming, infectious pop-punk bounce at 98 BPM.

sectionProgressions.description: Billie Joe's crunching downstroke power chords over Mike Dirnt's melodic, rolling bassline
Steady, relaxed downstroke rhythm with light palm muting on the downbeats
'You can't go forcing something if it's just not right...' - unmuted power chords ringing with anthemic clarity
Dynamic departure climbing through A5 and C5 before holding an emphatic D5 dominant chord into the guitar solo

harmonicFunction: G5 (I) - Warm, resonant tonic chord establishing the upbeat, melodic key center
D5 (V) - Dominant chord providing forward momentum across the 5th string
Em (vi) - Relative minor chord injecting subtle melancholy into the pop-punk bounce
C5 (IV) - Subdominant chord providing uplifting resolution back to tonic G5
A5 (ii) - Supertonic chord creating emotional tension in the bridge buildup

techniques.name: Syncopated Downstroke Power Chords
techniques.description: Executing clean, punchy power chords with steady pick-hand downstrokes while letting the open B and high E strings ring subtly on the upbeats for chiming harmonic resonance

notes: Fret standard root-5th-octave power chords on the 6th and 5th strings
Relax fret-hand fingers slightly to mute the unplayed strings, or let strings 1 and 2 ring open for Green Day's signature chime
Maintain relaxed wrist motion at 98 BPM without tensing the forearm
Accentuate the syncopated push on beat 2-and during chord transitions
sequence: Downstroke G5 on fret 3 of low E string
Shift to D5 on fret 5 of A string with crisp pick attack
Drop to open E minor or E5 power chord on fret 7 of A string
Resolve onto C5 on fret 3 of A string
tips: Tune down one half-step (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb) to match the studio recording
Use a medium pick (0.73mm to 0.88mm Dunlop Tortex) for crisp cut and flexible strumming attack
Billie Joe used 'Blue' (his legendary Fernandes Strat copy with a slanted Seymour Duncan JB humbucker)

techniques.name: Melodic Pop-Punk Solo Phrasing
techniques.description: Playing a vocal, singable lead guitar solo based on the major pentatonic scale, utilizing expressive whole-step bends and unison ring to echo the vocal melody

notes: Target chord tones (thirds and fifths) rather than shredding fast pentatonic scales
Execute full-step bends on fret 14 of the G string up to the root note
Add wide, relaxed finger vibrato at the peak of sustained bends
Let adjacent strings ring together during double-stop releases for garage-rock character
sequence: Slide up to fret 12 on the G string
Execute a full-step bend on fret 14 with the ring finger, supported by middle and index
Release the bend cleanly to fret 12, then land on fret 14 of the D string
End the phrase with a bluesy slide down the neck
tips: Think like a singer: ensure every note sustains with full emotion before shifting
Slightly boost the midrange on your amplifier or overdrive pedal to help the solo cut through
Do not over-bend: intonation is critical for the sweet pop-punk melody
details.progression: Solo over G5 - D5 - Em - C5

sections.name: Intro Signature Four-Chord Groove
sections.description: The quintessential mid-90s pop-punk opening: Billie Joe's crunching Fernandes Stratocaster delivers the unforgettable G5 - D5 - Em - C5 progression over Dirnt's melodic bass at 98 BPM.
notes: Steady downstroke eighth-note attack
Syncopated push on the upbeat into each new chord
Allow the open high strings to catch naturally on upbeat strums
Lock into the relaxed 98 BPM pocket

sections.name: Verse 1 Relaxed Palm-Muted Comping
sections.description: 'I heard you crying loud, all the way across town...' - steady, rhythmic downstroke power chords with subtle palm muting underneath Billie Joe's distinctive vocal.
notes: Apply light palm muting to downbeats
Open up muting on beat 4 for dynamic breathing room
Maintain clean string separation without excess fret noise
Keep the pick hand relaxed to prevent forearm tension

sections.name: Chorus Unmuted Stadium Hook
sections.description: 'You can't go forcing something if it's just not right...' - the band opens up into full, unmuted power-chord glory.
notes: Full unmuted power chords ringing across the stereo field
Dig in with aggressive pick attack for maximum Marshall crunch
Lock in with Tré Cool's solid backbeat snare
Seamless return to verse dynamic level

sections.name: Bridge Harmonic Buildup
sections.description: 'No time to search the world around, cause you know where I'll be found...' - dynamic harmonic lift moving through A5 and C5, holding on an extended D5.
notes: Sharp downstroke power-chord stabs on A5 and C5
Driving sixteenth-note crescendo on the D5 dominant chord
Tré Cool executes a rolling snare build underneath
Explosive release into the guitar solo

sections.name: Melodic Guitar Solo
sections.description: Billie Joe plays one of the catchiest, most singable guitar solos in 1990s rock: a melodic masterclass of expressive bends, open-string ring, and vocal phrasing.
notes: Whole-step bend on fret 14 of the G string up to A
Singing vibrato at the peak of each sustained phrase
Let adjacent strings ring slightly for raw garage-rock bite
Slide down into the final verse entrance
sections.exerciseLabel: Billie Joe Armstrong Melodic Solo Masterclass

sections.name: Outro Climax & Ringing Resolution
sections.description: Final chorus repetition with ad-lib vocal shouts, culminating in a ringing G5 power chord that sustains with warm tube feedback.
notes: Maximum energetic strumming assault
Lock in with the final crashing cymbal accents
Hold final G5 chord with natural amplifier sustain
Clean, ringing studio resolution

guitar.recommended: Fernandes Stratocaster copy ('Blue') or Fender Stratocaster with bridge humbucker
guitar.pickup: Slanted bridge humbucker (Seymour Duncan JB) for punchy, cutting midrange

amp.recommended: Marshall 100W Super Lead Plexi (1959SLP modified by Bob Bradshaw/Martin Golub, 'Pete')

effects.distortion: Cranked Marshall tube crunch (no external boost or overdrive pedal needed)
effects.other: MXR Carbon Copy analog delay on guitar solo for subtle depth

beginner.title: Half-Step Down Tuning & Power Chords
steps: Tune your guitar half-step down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)
Learn the G5, D5, Em, and C5 power chord shapes

intermediate.title: Rhythm Dynamics & Bridge Transition
steps: Master the light palm muting on the verse downbeats
Execute the bridge progression (A5 - C5 - D5) with dynamic build
Maintain steady downstroke timing without rushing the tempo

advanced.title: The Melodic Solo & Full Performance
steps: Transcribe and perform the singable guitar solo note-for-note
Nail the whole-step bends and vocal wrist vibrato
Perform the entire 2:58 track locked with bass and drums

commonMistakes: Playing in standard tuning instead of tuning down one half-step (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)
Tensing the pick-hand wrist and arm during repetitive downstrokes
Over-bending notes in the guitar solo, ruining the sweet vocal melody
Rushing the relaxed, breezy 98 BPM groove
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Half-step down tuning check and gentle wrist warm-up
10 mins: Metronome practice of the main four-chord progression at 80, 90, and 98 BPM
10 mins: Bridge dynamic build drills focusing on the D5 dominant hold
10 mins: Solo transcription study focusing on intonation of whole-step bends
focusAreas: Fret-hand finger economy during power chord shifts
Pick-hand downstroke consistency and wrist relaxation
Melodic bend accuracy and singing vibrato in the solo
metronomeWork: Set your metronome to 98 BPM to lock in the relaxed pop-punk groove
Practice picking strictly on the eighth-note grid to develop rock-solid timing
Isolate the transition from the D5 chord into the guitar solo
